sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.84% (-43 bp in a month), 2-year 4.46% (-33 bp); 2s10s curve +38 bp (-10 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 3.99% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.96 (-0.3% in a month, +3.7% YTD). USD/BRL 5.487 (+10.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.660 (-0.7%); USD/MXN 18.71 (+4.1%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -5.9% in a month (+7.4% YTD); VIX 26.8. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

us_econ: Inflation: CPI 3.7% y/y (2026-09), core 2.6%; core 3-month annualized 3.4%; core PCE 3.1%. Jobs: payrolls +29k in 2026-09 (3-month average +51k), unemployment 4.2% (+0.1), wages 3.0% y/y. Growth: real GDP 3.4% annualized in 2026-Q3, consumer spending 3.8%. Policy: fed funds target 3.75-4.0% (effective 3.88%); 2-year Treasury 4.46% (+0.58 vs fed funds: market pricing hikes); 10-year breakeven inflation 2.24%, real 10-year 2.60%. Farm prices (PPI farm products) +1.5% y/y; food-at-home CPI +1.8% y/y. For ags: high real yields and a firm dollar weigh on fund demand for commodities; sticky inflation keeps rates high (carry and storage costs up); a weak job market or falling real incomes hits meat and dairy demand first.

energy.read: Gas storage 3,801 Bcf (week to 2026-10-30), +77 Bcf vs a 5-year average +36 for the week; +40 Bcf (+1.1%) vs the 5-year average, -104 vs last year. Crude stocks 409.8 mb (-0.9 mb on the week, -5.2% vs 5-yr avg); gasoline -0.2 mb, distillate -3.6 mb; refinery utilization 94.5%. 3-2-1 crack $47.98/bbl (ULSD $92.28, gasoline $25.83). Options: NG IV 68% vs RV 50%; CL IV 56% vs RV 56%; HO IV 65% vs RV 51%; RB IV 53% vs RV 38%. For ags: diesel and natural gas set farm fuel, drying and nitrogen fertilizer costs; crude and gasoline drive ethanol and biodiesel margins (corn, soybean oil).
